ops.title: No spawn-dependent test result from yasyf's box is evidence: exec latency swings four orders of magnitude with load
ops.body:
Measured 2026-07-30 while landing the rewrite's phase 0, and it settles a question that has now
misled three separate investigations.

## The measurement

Same command, same box, minutes apart:

    /bin/sh -c 'exit 0'   during 3 concurrent worktree lanes:  2.74s 7.07s 13.66s 1.27s 4.62s
    /bin/sh -c :          with the box idle:                   0.00s 0.00s 0.00s
    /bin/zsh -c :         idle:                                0.00s 0.00s 0.00s
    /bin/bash -c :        idle:                                0.00s 0.00s 0.00s
    a freshly-built unsigned Go binary, idle:                  0.25s 0.25s 0.25s

Load average was 2.06 with 513 uid processes during the SLOW readings — a low load average, so
this is not ordinary CPU contention. It is bursty and it is worst during concurrent build/test
lanes, exactly when a verification wave wants to run.

Two separate effects, do not conflate them:

1. **Exec latency under concurrent lanes is unbounded in practice** — 0ms to 13.66s for the same
   trivial spawn. This reproduces the A1 lane's independent finding (a raw two-line shell script
   measured 1.77s to 31.76s on this box) and the plan's earlier note (3.3s to 11.9s at 694-754
   uid processes).
2. **A freshly-built unsigned Go binary costs ~250ms per exec where a shell costs ~0ms**, and
   that one IS consistent rather than bursty. Roughly 50x a normal exec. Consistent with per-exec
   provenance/signature evaluation on an unsigned binary, though the cause is not proven — the
   box also runs a Kandji Endpoint Security system extension (io.kandji.KandjiAgent.ESF-Extension,
   activated) and a SentinelOne network extension. Relevant to open task 72313e5 (cask-installed
   daemonkit binaries hanging pre-main when kernel provenance-tracked); not chased further.

## The standing rule

**A spawn-dependent test result from this machine is never evidence, in either direction.** Not a
pass, not a failure. That covers proc, service, worker, daemon and trust — every suite that
spawns. CI or a provably quiet machine is the gate, which is what the remediation plan already
required and what keeps getting forgotten under time pressure.

Corollary for triage: a `worker: timed out` / `timed out waiting for path .../active` /
`trust verifier self-probe failed` signature on this box carries NO information about the code.
Three investigations have now spent time on it — backlog 243d40c, de7d5ca5 and 29a01afd are three
vantage points on it, the mixed-era gate's pre-cut fixture flake (~1 start in 5) is a fourth, and
the phase-0 lanes rediscovered it a fifth time.

## Why this matters more than a flaky-test note

`proc/manager.go:1139` spawns EVERY daemonkit child through `exec.Command("/bin/sh", ...)` — the
`childWrapper` spawn gate. The trust verifier child then pays it twice: once for the sh wrapper,
once for the unsigned `os.Executable()` re-exec. So daemonkit's own hot paths are maximally
exposed to precisely the cost this measures, which is why the "verifier takes 1.78-2.69s" figure
looked like a daemonkit cost for months and was not one.

The rewrite deletes both independently — the `/bin/sh` gate becomes POSIX_SPAWN_START_SUSPENDED,
and peer verification becomes kernel-only with no child at all (note bfc1789). Neither change was
argued on this basis, and both are worth more than their own justifications claimed.

## Base-commit status, for the record

At 0e60747 the `worker` suite FAILS locally with this signature (TestRunChildInheritsParentPath,
TestCloseJoinsEveryAdmittedRun, TestQueueCapacityIsNonblockingAndDeadlineCoversQueue and 8 more,
all spawn-deadline shaped). All seven CI workflows were green on that same commit, and a lane
proved the failures reproduce with the new phase-0 package physically removed from the tree.
Pre-existing and environmental. Do not attribute it to the rewrite, and do not "fix" it.
